newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila will keep sugar export quota to U.S.
newsitem.headline: Manila will keep sugar export quota to U.S.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Monday that Manila would maintain its sugar export quota to the United States.
"We will maintain the (U.S.) sugar quota and we will try to fulfill that quota," Ramos said in his weekly news conference.
Last month, Philippine Sugar Regulatory Administration chief Wilson Gamboa asked Ramos to order a stop to the country's sugar exports to the United States beginning crop year 1997/1998 (Sept/Aug).
The Philippines is a beneficiary of a U.S. sugar import programme under which it buys the commodity from developing countries at premium prices.
Gamboa had said the Philippines should stop its U.S. sugar exports so it need not import from other countries to meet its own domestic requirements.
The Philippines had an average 250,000 tonne sugar shortage over each of the past three years with harvests at 1.75 million tonnes.
The Philippine Sugar Millers Association had said the country should continue to maintain its U.S. sugar exports despite a shortage on domestic harvests.
The Philippines was granted a sugar quota of 246,411 tonnes for crop year 1996/1997.
